subject: science

entries: Central dogma: DNA makes protein: DNA is transcribed into mRNA in the nucleus, and the mRNA is translated into a polypeptide at a ribosome.
slots.label: Central dogma
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Monohybrid cross: the 3:1 ratio: Aa x Aa gives genotypes 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa in the Punnett square, which group into phenotypes in the ratio 3:1.
slots.label: Monohybrid cross
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Dihybrid cross: 9:3:3:1: two genes on different chromosomes assort independently, so sixteen boxes give four phenotype classes in the ratio 9:3:3:1.
slots.label: Dihybrid cross
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Sex-linked inheritance: a gene on the X chromosome is passed from a carrier mother to half her sons, who show the trait because the Y cannot mask it.
slots.label: Sex-linked inheritance
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: mutations are always harmful: most sequence changes are neutral because the protein still does its job, so harm is the exception, not the rule.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The molecule that stores genetic instructions as a sequence of bases, organised into genes on chromosomes.
slots.label: DNA
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A length of DNA that codes for one polypeptide chain.
slots.label: Gene
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: One of the alternative forms of a gene, found at the same locus on homologous chromosomes.
slots.label: Allele
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The alleles an organism carries for a gene, such as AA, Aa or aa.
slots.label: Genotype
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The observable trait an organism shows, produced by its genotype and environment.
slots.label: Phenotype
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An allele that shows in the phenotype whenever it is present, even in a heterozygote.
slots.label: Dominant allele
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An allele that shows in the phenotype only when no dominant allele is present.
slots.label: Recessive allele
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A change in the DNA base sequence; most mutations are neutral, some are harmful, and a rare few are beneficial.
slots.label: Mutation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
